listing.name: Daytona USA (Sega Model 2 arcade) (Daytona USA static recompilation)
listing.summary: Documented Windows Daytona USA arcade source-build route for your own daytona93 or daytona ROM set. Choose the completed matching native build; upstream/player owns rebuilding and separate per-set profiles.

steps.title: Complete the documented upstream build deliberately
steps.instruction: Use source and components you are independently permitted to use. This route has no observed public runtime release: finish the documented Windows setup/source build outside Portcove before registration. Upstream setup can install Visual Studio C++/Clang and other development tools and fetch pinned dependencies; review that activity yourself. A source checkout or generated C++ alone is not a completed player. Keep the complete working project, build outputs, supplied runtime companions and notices.

steps.title: Supply the exact arcade ROM set for that build
steps.instruction: Use your own MAME-format daytona93.zip/.7z for Daytona USA Deluxe ’93, or daytona.zip/.7z for Revision A (1994), with the upstream-required members. These are separate compiled variants, not interchangeable input names. The source has per-file size and CRC checks for the selected set, including the different program/sound ROMs; a matching filename alone is insufficient and CRC is not cryptographic entitlement or whole-archive authentication. Keep all original archives unchanged. Console Daytona titles and other arcade revisions are outside this guide.

steps.title: Add the actual completed Windows player
steps.instruction: Select the matching completed daytona.exe from the output location printed by upstream setup: normally build/Release/daytona.exe (or build/daytona.exe with Ninja) for daytona93, and the corresponding build-daytona/ output for Revision A. Use the project root containing roms/ and those build folders as working directory. Supply --rom and the absolute path to your own matching archive as two literal arguments. The native process owns both its launcher and game loop. If your established setup also uses --profile <name>, preserve that exact profile argument. Do not select a setup/recompile script, test/oracle executable or another variant. Saving launch details and Play are separate actions.

steps.title: Preserve separate settings and runtime ownership
steps.instruction: Upstream/player owns toolchain setup, ROM generation, rebuilding and runtime replacement. Windows settings, EEPROM, backup RAM and logs use %APPDATA%/daytona-recomp/daytona93 or daytona, with a separate <set>-<profile> folder when --profile is used; preserve launcher.ini, ioboard_eeprom.bin, backup_ram.bin, daytona.log and every active profile. Retain the entire working project, originals and old complete player before updating/rebuilding, then review/relink changed selected bytes. Revision A’s initial twin-cabinet configuration may require upstream Test mode to choose a single cabinet; no network/link/wheel acceptance is supplied. Removing registration preserves external files; Portcove does not own backups, rollback, save migration, compatibility or deletion.

warnings: Pinned source and documented build contract only. No ROM archive, generated source/output, compiled player, package integrity, native game, real save, hardware renderer, link play or device qualification was executed. Source BSD3 and separate component terms do not grant Sega ROM rights; actual independently permitted source/components/originals remain required.
